newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cold dealys planting, growth - Met Office.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cold dealys planting, growth - Met Office.

text.p: Unusually cold weather in Hungary this month will delay maize and potato planting and also put back wheat and barley growth by up to two weeks, the Hungarian Meteorological Office (OMSZ) said on Tuesday.
"Wheat growth has already been delayed by an estimated two weeks," Attila Bussay of the OMSZ's agricultural department told Reuters.
The mean temperature for the April 1 to 20 period was four degrees Celsius below the average. He said two to three degrees below average already amounted to "extremely cold weather".
Bussay said soil temperature remained well below the eight to 10 degrees Celsius needed for potato planting and the 10 to 14 degrees for maize planting.
"One can gamble to a certain extent with planting maize despite the cold, but with potato that would be extremely risky," he said.
This could be the coldest April in Hungary this century.
Temperatures below freezing point were registered in recent days and there had been scattered snowfalls across the country since Sunday.
However, precipitation did not reach the seasonal average and the drought was an additional drawback for agriculture.
Grains prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange have been on the rise for the last two weeks, which traders said was due to both local factors and international trends.
FOT (free on truck) maize prices currently stand at 18,000 forints for maize and 26,000 forints for milling wheat despite significant rollover stocks and limited export possibilities.
